as_told.title: Pentagon review of Vera Rubin Observatory imagery
as_told.place_text: Vera Rubin Observatory; secure facility in California

plain: This story is about the Vera Rubin Observatory, a large telescope that photographs the night sky, in the 2020s. An astronomer named Beatriz Villarroel, speaking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, passes on what she says she was told. She says the telescope is going to remove many classified satellites and other objects from its data. Classified here means secret, run by governments and not made public. Months later, Michels comes back to it on his own show. He says all of the observatory's images have to be approved by the Pentagon, the US defence department, at a secure site in California, and he credits this to an article in The Atlantic magazine. If true, it would mean that what the public gets to see of the sky is filtered to hide certain objects in orbit.
